== Problem ==

Amy, Bomani, Charlie, and Daria work in a chocolate factory. On Monday Amy, Bomani, and Charlie started working at <imath>1:00 \ \mathrm{PM}</imath> and were able to pack <imath>4</imath>, <imath>3</imath>, and <imath>3</imath> packages, respectively, every <imath>3</imath> minutes. At some later time, Daria joined the group, and Daria was able to pack <imath>5</imath> packages every <imath>4</imath> minutes. Together, they finished packing <imath>450</imath> packages at exactly <imath>2:45\ \mathrm{PM}</imath>. At what time did Daria join the group?

<imath>\textbf{(A) }1:25\text{ PM}\qquad\textbf{(B) }1:35\text{ PM}\qquad\textbf{(C) }1:45\text{ PM}\qquad\textbf{(D) }1:55\text{ PM}\qquad\textbf{(E) }2:05\text{ PM}</imath>

== Solution 1 ==

Note that Amy, Bomani, and Charlie pack a total of <imath>4+3+3=10</imath> packages every <imath>3</imath> minutes.

The total amount of time worked is <imath>1</imath> hour and <imath>45</imath> minutes, which when converted to minutes, is <imath>105</imath> minutes. This means that since Amy, Bomani, and Charlie worked for the entire <imath>105</imath> minutes, they in total packed <imath>\dfrac{105}{3}\cdot10=350</imath> packages.

Since <imath>450</imath> packages were packed in total, then Daria must have packed <imath>450-350=100</imath> packages in total, and since she packs at a rate of <imath>5</imath> packages per <imath>4</imath> minutes, then Daria worked for <imath>\dfrac{100}{5}\cdot4=80</imath> minutes, therefore Daria joined <imath>80</imath> minutes before <imath>2:45</imath> PM, which was at <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(A) }1:25\text{ PM}}</imath>.

~Tacos_are_yummy_1, andliu766

== Solution 2 ==

Let the time, in minutes, elapsed between <imath>1:00</imath> and the time Daria joined the packaging be <imath>x</imath>. Since Amy packages <imath>4</imath> packages every <imath>3</imath> minutes, she packages <imath>\frac{4}{3}</imath> packages per minute. Similarly, we can see that both Bomani and Charlie package <imath>1</imath> package per minute, and Daria packages <imath>\frac{5}{4}</imath> packages every minute.

Before Daria arrives, we can write the total packages packaged as <imath>x(\frac{4}{3} + 1 + 1) = x(\frac{10}{3})</imath>. Since there are <imath>105</imath> minutes between <imath>1:00</imath> and <imath>2:45</imath>, Daria works with the other three for <imath>105-x</imath> minutes, meaning for that time there are <imath>(105-x)(\frac{4}{3} + 1 + 1 + \frac{5}{4}) = (105-x)(\frac{55}{12})</imath> packages packaged. 

Adding the two, we get <imath>x(\frac{10}{3}) + (105-x)(\frac{55}{12}) = 450</imath> (The total packaged in the entire time is <imath>450</imath>). Solving this equation, we get <imath>x=25</imath>, meaning Daria arrived <imath>25</imath> minutes after <imath>1:00</imath>, meaning the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(A) }1:25\text{ PM}}</imath>.

~i_am_suk_at_math_2
